title: Advanced Passive: Reporting Verbs, Impersonal Structures & Complex Forms
grammarTitle: Advanced Passive Structures: Reporting, Impersonal & Complex
grammarNote: На уровне B1-B2 пассивный залог становится инструментом точной, нюансированной коммуникации. Здесь мы изучаем три продвинутые структуры: пассив с глаголами сообщения (it is said that / he is believed to be), безличные конструкции (it is known / it has been established), и комплексные пассивные формы с инфинитивом.

grammarTable.subject: It is said that...
grammarTable.example: "It is said that the discovery changed medicine forever." (people say this)

grammarTable.subject: He is said to be...
grammarTable.example: "He is said to be the best candidate." / "She is believed to have left."

grammarTable.subject: It has been established that
grammarTable.example: "It has been established that smoking causes cancer." (scientific proof)

grammarTable.subject: It is thought / believed / reported
grammarTable.example: "It is thought that thousands were affected." (uncertainty hedged by passive)

grammarTable.subject: be + supposed to
grammarTable.example: "You are supposed to submit by Friday." (expectation) / "It's supposed to work." (expectation it will)

grammarTable.subject: have something done
grammarTable.example: "She had her essay proofread." / "I need to have my laptop repaired."

grammarExtra.title: Reporting verbs in passive — two structures

rows.form: Structure A: IT + passive + that clause
rows.example: "It IS SAID THAT he is the best researcher." / "It WAS REPORTED THAT errors had been made." ✅
"He IS SAID TO BE the best researcher." / "She IS BELIEVED TO HAVE LEFT." ✅

rows.form: Common verbs: say / report / believe / think / know / expect / claim / understand
rows.example: "It IS KNOWN THAT..." / "He IS EXPECTED TO..." / "She WAS UNDERSTOOD TO HAVE..." ✅
"She is believed TO HAVE DISCOVERED the error." (she already discovered it — past relative to "is believed") ✅
"The contract is expected TO BE SIGNED next week." (passive infinitive) ✅

rows.form: Why use it: avoiding naming sources
rows.example: "It is reported that..." = "people say / sources say" — without naming who. ✅

grammarExtra.title: Impersonal passive — expressing consensus and established facts

rows.example: "It is widely accepted that climate change is human-caused." (broad agreement) ✅
"It has been demonstrated that sleep deprivation impairs performance." (proven) ✅
"It is generally understood that early intervention improves outcomes." ✅
"It has long been known that exercise has mental health benefits." ✅
They suggest "the scientific community agrees" rather than "I personally think." ✅
"It is firmly established" > "It is generally accepted" > "It has been suggested" ✅

grammarExtra.title: Be supposed to — expectation and obligation

rows.example: "You are SUPPOSED TO submit by Friday." (expectation — maybe you haven't yet) ✅
"He wasn't SUPPOSED TO know about the meeting." (but he did) ✅
"The meeting WAS SUPPOSED TO start at 3. It started at 4." (expectation not met) ✅
"Should" = advice/obligation. "Supposed to" = expectation (often from an external source) ✅
"She had her essay PROOFREAD." (someone else proofread it for her) ✅
"I need to get my laptop REPAIRED." = causative get. Someone repairs it for me. ✅
"I'm having my phone FIXED." / "She had her car SERVICED." / "I need to have this CHECKED." ✅
"He had his wallet STOLEN." (he didn't arrange it — it happened to him) ✅

rows.form: Subject does NOT do the action
rows.example: "She had her portrait PAINTED BY a local artist." — the artist painted, not she. ✅

rows.form: ✗ "It is said he is the best." (missing "that")
rows.example: ✅ "It is said THAT he is the best." — "that" is required. ✅
✅ "He is supposed to HAVE LEFT." — infinitive form, not past. ✅

rows.form: ✗ "She got her essay written by herself."
rows.example: ✅ Causative implies someone else does it. "By herself" = she did it = not causative. ✅

rows.form: ✗ "It is established that X is Y." (too strong)
rows.example: ✅ Use "it has been established" (PP) or "it is widely established" to signal appropriate certainty. ✅

grammarTip:
Advanced Passive Structures:

REPORTING VERBS — 2 structures:
A: It IS SAID THAT he is the best.
B: He IS SAID TO BE the best.

With past reference:
"She IS BELIEVED TO HAVE DISCOVERED the error."
(present belief about past action → perfect infinitive)

IMPERSONAL PASSIVE for scientific consensus:
"It HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED that..."
"It IS WIDELY ACCEPTED that..."
"It HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED that..."

BE SUPPOSED TO = expectation:
"You ARE SUPPOSED TO submit by Friday."
"The meeting WAS SUPPOSED TO start at 3."
(expectation, often not met)

CAUSATIVE (have/get something done):
have + obj + pp
"She HAD her essay PROOFREAD."
"I need to GET my laptop REPAIRED."
→ Someone else does it for you

exercises.text: "People say he is the most qualified candidate." → It ___ he is the most qualified candidate.
exercises.hint: "IT IS SAID THAT he is the most qualified candidate." Structure A: It + passive + that clause. ✅

exercises.text: "People believe she is the best researcher." → She ___ (believe) the best researcher.
exercises.hint: "She IS BELIEVED TO BE the best researcher." Structure B: subject + passive + to-infinitive. ✅

exercises.text: "It is thought that she has already submitted." → She ___ already submitted.
exercises.hint: Past action before present belief → PERFECT INFINITIVE: "She IS THOUGHT TO HAVE ALREADY SUBMITTED." ✅

exercises.text: "Scientists have demonstrated that sleep deprivation harms performance." → ___ sleep deprivation harms performance.
exercises.hint: "IT HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED THAT..." — Present Perfect impersonal passive for established fact. ✅

exercises.text: "The meeting was supposed to ___ at 3, but it didn't start until 4."
exercises.hint: "was supposed TO START" — was supposed to + base infinitive. (Expectation that wasn't met.) ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ her laptop repaired yesterday." (someone repaired it for her)
exercises.hint: "She HAD her laptop REPAIRED." — causative: have + obj + pp. Someone else repaired it for her. ✅

exercises.text: "I need to ___ my essay ___ (proofread) before submitting."
exercises.hint: "I need to GET my essay PROOFREAD." — causative get: get + obj + pp. Someone else proofreads it. ✅

exercises.text: "He wasn't supposed to ___ the password." (but he did know it)
exercises.hint: "He wasn't SUPPOSED TO KNOW the password." = expected not to know. ✅ (Plain infinitive after "supposed to")

exercises.text: "While he was travelling, he ___ his phone stolen."
exercises.hint: "He HAD his phone STOLEN." or "He GOT his phone STOLEN." — causative for negative experience (it happened TO him). Both ✅.

exercises.text: "It ___ that the company lost millions." (news now, referring to recent event)
opts: Both "is reported" and "is being reported" work
exercises.correct: Both "is reported" and "is being reported" work
exercises.hint: "IT IS REPORTED THAT..." (established, current report) / "IT IS BEING REPORTED..." (actively happening in news now). Both ✅.

exercises.text: "___ (it / widely / accept) that early education improves long-term outcomes."
exercises.hint: "IT IS WIDELY ACCEPTED THAT early education improves long-term outcomes." Impersonal passive. ✅

exercises.instruction: "She is expected to..." — future or present?
exercises.text: "She is expected to present her findings next month." — "is expected to present" means:
opts: People expect her to present (future plan)
exercises.correct: People expect her to present (future plan)
exercises.hint: "is expected to" = people expect this will happen. Future expectation via passive. ✅

exercises.text: "It is said he discovered the element last year."
opts: "It is said" needs "that" — "It is said THAT he discovered..."
exercises.correct: "It is said" needs "that" — "It is said THAT he discovered..."
exercises.hint: ✅ "It IS SAID THAT he discovered the element last year." — "that" is required. ✅

exercises.instruction: Degree of certainty in impersonal passive.
opts: "It has been firmly established that X."
exercises.correct: "It has been firmly established that X."
exercises.hint: "firmly established" = strongest/most certain. "suggested" and "proposed" = tentative. "thought" = uncertain opinion. ✅

exercises.text: "I'm ___ my apartment ___ (redecorate) next month." (future plan, someone else does it)
exercises.correct: having / redecorated / going to have redecorated
exercises.hint: "I'm HAVING my apartment REDECORATED." OR "I'm going to HAVE my apartment REDECORATED." ✅ (Both acceptable for future plan)

exercises.instruction: Which is NOT a valid use of "be supposed to"?
exercises.text: Choose the incorrect or unnatural sentence.
opts: "The results are supposed to be announced today." (expectation)
"He was supposed to call but didn't." (unmet expectation)
exercises.hint: ✗ "She is supposed to VERY CLEVER." — Missing "be." ✅ "She is supposed to BE very clever." ✅

questions.text: "It is said that he is the best." — This structure is:
questions.hint: "It + passive reporting verb + that clause" = Structure A impersonal reporting. ✅

questions.text: "People believe she has already discovered the error." → She ___ already discovered the error.
questions.hint: Structure B: "She IS BELIEVED TO HAVE already discovered." Perfect infinitive for past action. ✅

questions.text: "It has been established that smoking causes cancer." — This passive expresses:
questions.hint: "It HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED" = scientific community has proven this. Community consensus. ✅

questions.text: "She had her essay proofread." — "had her essay proofread" means:
questions.hint: Causative: have + object + pp = someone else did the action. She arranged for it. ✅

questions.text: "You are supposed to submit by Friday." — "supposed to" expresses:
opts: An expectation or obligation (often from an external source)
questions.correct: An expectation or obligation (often from an external source)
questions.hint: "be supposed to" = expected to (by external rules/expectations). ✅

questions.text: "He is believed to have left the country." — "to have left" is:
opts: Perfect infinitive — the leaving is past relative to the present belief
questions.correct: Perfect infinitive — the leaving is past relative to the present belief
questions.hint: "to have left" = perfect infinitive. The leaving (past) is earlier than the believing (present). ✅

questions.text: "It is said he discovered X." — What is missing?
opts: "that" — "It is said THAT he discovered X."
questions.correct: "that" — "It is said THAT he discovered X."
questions.hint: ✅ "It is said THAT he discovered X." — "that" is required in Structure A. ✅

questions.text: "She was supposed to call at 3." — This implies:
opts: There was an expectation she would call — possibly she didn't
questions.correct: There was an expectation she would call — possibly she didn't
questions.hint: "Was supposed to" = expectation (in the past), often implying it wasn't met. ✅

opts: "It has been firmly established that X."
questions.correct: "It has been firmly established that X."
questions.hint: "firmly established" = strongest. "thought" and "suggested" = weaker, more tentative. ✅

questions.text: "He had his car stolen while on holiday." — "had his car stolen" is:
opts: Negative experience passive (it happened TO him)
questions.correct: Negative experience passive (it happened TO him)
questions.hint: Causative CAN describe negative experiences that weren't arranged. "Had his car stolen" = it happened to him. ✅

questions.text: "The results ___ (expect) to be published by the end of the month."
questions.hint: "The results ARE EXPECTED TO BE PUBLISHED." Structure B (subject + passive + to-infinitive). ✅

opts: "It is widely accepted climate change is real."
"It is widely accepted that climate change is real."
"It widely accepts that climate change is real."
"It was widely accepted that climate change has been real."
questions.correct: "It is widely accepted that climate change is real."
questions.hint: "IT IS WIDELY ACCEPTED THAT climate change is real." — impersonal passive + "that" + clause. ✅
